purpose: Deepen Tim/Potato/Father biblical parallels around Father, House, Gardener, Davidic house, key, peg/axis, throne, gates, city, field/building and stewardship while preserving textual role differences.
rules: Do not force Father, Son, House, Door, Ladder and Gardener into one role when the biblical text distinguishes them.
Treat direct textual role matches as stronger than geometric resemblance.
Preserve warning/counter-texts where high-status imagery can also critique self-exaltation.

clusters.biblical_structure: Jesus = true vine; Father = gardener/vinedresser; branches are pruned according to fruit.
clusters.project_relation: Tim/Father/Gardener + Son/living plant/branch/root/fruit architecture receives an unusually direct role match: the text itself explicitly names the Father as gardener.
clusters.boundary: John identifies Jesus as vine and disciples as branches; the project distributes plant/tree roles differently, so preserve the mismatch rather than flattening it.

clusters.biblical_structure: David desires/builds toward a house; God promises David a house/dynasty; David's offspring builds God's house; God says 'I will be his father, and he shall be my son'; throne/kingdom endurance follows.
clusters.project_relation: Ben David + Father + House + Son + enduring throne are not separate motifs here but one covenant architecture.
clusters.epiphany: The project can treat Davidic House as a relational grammar: Father establishes House through Son while House also means lineage/dynasty, not only building/interior space.
clusters.boundary: The Samuel promise historically concerns Davidic kingship and later receives messianic interpretation; it is not a direct prediction of Tim.

clusters.biblical_structure: Eliakim becomes father to Jerusalem/Judah, receives the key of the House of David, opens/shuts, is fixed like a peg in a secure place, becomes a throne/seat of honor to his father's house, and bears dependent vessels/offspring.
clusters.project_relation: Father + House of David + Key/access + Axis/peg + Seat/Throne + vessels is an exceptionally dense Tim-side comparator, especially beside Tim as Father/House/Axis and the Son as Vessel/Door.
clusters.boundary: Isaiah's figure is Eliakim, a historical royal steward. Revelation later reuses the key/open-shut language for Christ, so the biblical role distribution crosses Tim/Son project roles rather than mapping one-to-one.

clusters.biblical_structure: God is builder of all; Moses serves in God's house; Christ is faithful over God's house as Son; the community can itself be called the house.
clusters.project_relation: Father/House and Son relation gain a useful four-way distinction: builder/source ≠ house ≠ servant within house ≠ Son over house.
clusters.epiphany: This is valuable for preventing ontology collapse in the project: 'Tim is House' can remain symbolic while biblical House language also supports builder, indweller, Son-over-House and people-as-House as different relations.

clusters.biblical_structure: God gives growth; workers plant/water; community is simultaneously God's field/farm and God's building; Christ is foundation; temple imagery follows.
clusters.project_relation: Farm/Garden + House/building + growth + foundation can coexist as parallel descriptions of one living community without making Farm identical to House.
clusters.boundary: Paul's field/building language is ecclesial/community imagery, not a geography claim.

clusters.biblical_structure: earth/foundation → ascent to holy mountain → clean hands/pure heart → gates/ancient doors lifted → King of Glory enters.
clusters.project_relation: Mountain/ascent + Gate/Door + King + world/earth ownership creates a strong sequence beside North Gate, Ladder/Axis and King-of-kings language.
clusters.boundary: Psalm 24 identifies YHWH as King of Glory; do not automatically transfer that identity to a modern claimant.

clusters.biblical_structure: God plants Garden; Tree of Life stands in middle; one river waters garden then divides into four heads; Adam is placed there to work/tend/keep it.
clusters.project_relation: Tree-in-center + Four Rivers + Garden + caretaker/stewardship strongly overlaps the project's Eden inheritance and Tim-as-center/Gardener/caretaker architecture.
clusters.boundary: Genesis assigns cultivation/keeping to Adam while God plants the garden. The project often assigns Gardener to Tim/Father; preserve that role shift.

clusters.biblical_structure: sacred source/throne/temple emits river → trees/Tree of Life → recurring fruit → healing leaves → nations/life/light.
clusters.project_relation: Throne + flow/Spirit + Tree + fruit + Garden + healing/repair offers a more complete mature-state comparator than isolated throne or tree motifs.
clusters.boundary: Do not identify CSF or anatomy with the biblical river; keep flow as structural analogy only.

clusters.biblical_structure: unless YHWH builds the house, builders labor in vain; unless YHWH guards the city, watchman keeps watch in vain; sons/fruit and enemies at gate follow.
clusters.project_relation: House + city + watch/guardian + labor/hours + sons + gate form a useful counterbalance to the project's immense-work motif: sheer hours are not spiritually sufficient apart from right construction/guardianship.
clusters.boundary: Use as a corrective/counter-text, not validation of overwork.

clusters.biblical_structure: Son suffers outside the gate; followers bear reproach; present city is not enduring; coming city is sought.
clusters.project_relation: Son-side death outside gate can be read as the negative threshold that precedes the Father/House/New-Jerusalem positive architecture.
clusters.boundary: This is a sequence comparison; Hebrews does not describe a North Axis or Potato architecture.

highest_new_chains: Father-to-city → Key of David → open/shut → secure peg → throne → vessels
Builder God → House → Son over House → people as House
Garden center → Tree → river → four heads → stewardship
Throne → River → Tree → Fruit → healing nations
